text:
Sasha: heads-up — running Mistral-7B quant bakeoff (AWQ / GPTQ / 8-bit) across H100 + A100 fleets and hitting weird driver/kernel failures when routing to trt-llm backend on some nodes. stack traces below.

Jamal: can you paste the minimal repro and which container/driver?

Sasha: repro:
```
MODEL=mistral-7b-awq
BACKEND=trt-llm
CONTAINER=redwood/rl-infer:prod-cuda-14.2
CMD=python -m run_inference --model $MODEL --backend $BACKEND --batch 1 --seq 512
```
error: `invalid device function` then a segfault in tensorrt plugin init. Happens only on nodes with driver 535.*; nodes with 530.* are fine.

infra-bot: detected host patch: driver-upgrade started on pool-gpu-h100-eta-4 (nodes: h100-34 -> 535.86). Rolling window: 2026-03-18 04:12 UTC :tooling:deploy

Lee: saw something similar last week on A100 where Triton v2.11 changed how it loads dynamic kernels. For us it showed `cuLaunchKernel: misaligned grid` when AWQ int8 paths tried to use fused kernels.

Maria: quick data point — AWQ 4-bit->int4 packing triggers custom kernel paths that expect a specific compute capability. GPTQ path is using an alternative CUDA kernel that falls back to torch ops; that one survives but is slower. So AWQ + TRT-LLM is the only one failing hard for us.

Praveen: try forcing the fallback path: set env `TRTLLM_FORCE_TORCH_FALLBACK=1` or disable trt-llm plugin in runtime profile. also try disabling KV caching to reduce fused-kernel codegen.

Sasha: tried `TRTLLM_FORCE_TORCH_FALLBACK=1` — run completes but 4x slower, accuracy looks okay. GPTQ path still crashes when `use_tensorrt=true` with:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'nvinfer1::CudaError'
what(): CUDA error 98: invalid device function
```

Jamal: 98 usually points to mismatched PTX vs driver or a kernel built for a higher arch than the device. Are we building TRT-LLM plugins at container build-time with a fixed -gencode arch?

Praveen: yes, our tensorrt plugin build uses `-gencode=compute_90,code=sm_90` for H100 and a fallback that includes sm_80/sm_86 for A100. But the new 535 driver tightened JIT/PTX compatibility; some nodes report different cudaComputeCapability values due to vendor BIOS patches.

Maria: workaround that worked for me: rebuild plugin with PTX + all sm codes, or instruct Triton to JIT compile PTX on the host. Example Docker step: 
```Dockerfile
RUN nvcc -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 \
    -ptx -o trt_plugin.ptx plugin.cu
```

Lee: for short-term, we should mark AWQ+TRT-LLM on driver 535+ as flaky. Add a test to CI that runs AWQ small-batch on canary nodes after driver upgrades.

Sasha: agree. Action items: (1) add a compat note to the quant matrix, (2) add a tiny reproducer in eng-ml/ci, (3) open infra ticket to pin driver or run plugin rebuild.

Jamal: I'll open a tracking issue and include the stack + exact node IDs and a small docker to reproduce. will also flag to platform to consider rebuilding trt-plugins at deploy time.

infra-bot: created ISSUE-ML-8721: "AWQ + TRT-LLM kernel failure on driver 535.*" — https://redwood-internal/ISSUE-ML-8721 :white_check_mark:

Praveen: adding one more note — vLLM path behaves differently because it uses torch kernels for attention permutation; if we want safe gradations in the matrix: AWQ+TRT-LLM = unsupported on 535.*, GPTQ+TRT-LLM = warn, AWQ+vLLM = supported (but slower). I'll draft a short compatibility table.

Sasha: perfect. I'll add a short sticky message in eng-ml summarizing the compatibility rules and link ISSUE-ML-8721. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

Maria: later we should add an automated smoke that runs every driver upgrade and checks all quant paths (AWQ/GPTQ/INT8) across backends (trt-llm, vLLM, triton) and reports diffs in token latency and pass/fail.

Lee: agreed. adding to roadmap: `quant-paths/driver-compat` canary job.

Jamal: tracking PR for reproducer + CI job will show up under the issue in ~2 days.

infra-bot: linked PR #4167 to ISSUE-ML-8721.
